records.region: Sonora, Mexico; northern feeder–Mazatán/Mátape corridor, Presa Ignacio R. Alatorre and lower San Marcial to the Empalme coastal setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the connected Mátape river system, including the selected unnamed northern feeder, locally named Mazatán reach, reservoir passage and lower San Marcial reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Full ordinary geographic correspondence is supported for FID 10248 over its complete route. The route begins on a western Villa Pesqueira feeder north of Presa La Hacienda, joins the valley toward Mazatán, follows the Mátape course through La Colorada and Presa Ignacio R. Alatorre, and continues as San Marcial to the Empalme coastal embayment. Río Mátape is supported as the representative system identity. The initial feeder, named local reaches, reservoir and lower river do not acquire one uniform scalar name.
records.completion_scope: Complete ordinary corridor correspondence of the northern feeder, Mazatán/Mátape reaches, reservoir passage, lower San Marcial and actual Empalme coastal terminal. Local names remain distinct from the representative system identity.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected Mátape river system, including the selected unnamed northern feeder, locally named Mazatán reach, reservoir passage and lower San Marcial reach.

component_scope_limits: The detailed northern map establishes a connected selected feeder, but does not justify naming its entire opening Mátape, El Encinito or any nearby label. Its local name remains null.
Río Mazatán is a map-supported local reach name, not automatically a whole-feature synonym.
La Colorada and Guaymas originals directly label the middle course Río Matape / Río Mátape.
Below Presa Ignacio R. Alatorre the original cartography labels the continuing river Río San Marcial / San Marcial.
The model ends at the Empalme coastal setting; the reservoir is an intermediate connection, not the selected terminal.
Mátape basin entries corroborate the representative system only after the original map route is established. No formal registry entry was independently established.
No current flow, navigation, reservoir shoreline, exact bank, vertex or legal name-transition boundary is asserted.

naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: The selection includes an unnamed headward feeder, Fletcher Creek, Boles Creek, a lower Willow Creek connection, the eastern Clear Lake reservoir/outlet setting, the mapped Lost River with impounded and channelized reaches, and an interior Tule Lake extension. Lost River is supported as representative system identity only. The representative name is not assigned to the upstream creeks or lake interiors. Exact hydronym-transition vertices, contemporary flow conditions and legal registry status remain unestablished.

records.completion_scope: The complete Inland Ice opening, upper eastward corridor, northern middle bend, southeastern descent, lower eastward approach and actual glaciated inner Umivik terminal setting are covered at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale. No representative natural-river identity, current glacier-front position or actual water routing is established.
records.region: Southeast Greenland; Inland Ice-to-glaciated inner Umivik coastal-margin corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: No supported representative natural-river identity. Umivik and adjacent coastal labels supply bounded geographic context only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The selected opening, long middle bends and lower approach occupy mapped Inland Ice and its glaciated coastal margin in the Umivik setting. The original cartography accounts for the complete selected corridor and actual terminal setting, but does not establish a natural-river identity. Ice contours, the nearby Umivik place label and adjacent coastal names are not river hydronyms.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The ending is read in the glaciated inner coastal setting west of the Umivik label, south of the Ikerssuaq / Køge Bugt coastal setting and north of Kap Møsting and Skjoldungen. These are cartographic geographic anchors, not names assigned to the modeled mainstem. The comparison concerns the actual selected ending, not merely the nearest large fjord or offshore label.

naming_scope_details.reason: Completed geographic setting correspondence and unresolved river-name scope are distinct. No retained source establishes a representative river identity.

records.supported_name_scope: Rio Anajás is repeatedly labeled along the middle and lower main channel. Igarapé Zinco is separately named on the selected headward approach. Igarapé da Praça, Mocões, Aramã, Guajará, Cururu, Jipuru and the island-side channels retain their own mapped scopes. No name is assigned to the unestablished initial connector.
records.completion_scope: Three selected mainstem fragments were read. The initial connector in FID11671 remains materially unestablished; the remaining Zinco–Anajás corridor, FIDs11672–11673, major side channels and actual terminal within the broad lower Rio Anajás are covered at ordinary generalized corridor scale.
records.region: Marajó Island, Pará, Brazil; selected Anajás river corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative downstream-system candidate; not a completed full-system identity or a uniform reach name.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected initial south-and-west connector in FID11671, south of Torre do Monte Alegre, is not established by either retained Anajás original. They show Igarapé Zinco and the separate Praça feeder and its farther-downstream joining, but not the selected southern connection. This is an unresolved hydrologic connector, not a demand for exact bank or vertex agreement. FIDs11672 and11673, and the remainder of FID11671, are read through the actual selected terminal.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected group follows an incompletely established initial feeder into Igarapé Zinco, then the Rio Anajás through Anajás town, the Guajará/Cururu joining region and broad lower anabranches beside Jipuru and Japichauá. Its selected terminal is still in the broad Rio Anajás channel east of Ilha das Guaribas near the Vila Monte/Charapucu setting; water continues north. The stored sea class does not establish an open-ocean mouth. Rio Anajás remains a provisional representative candidate because the opening connector is material pending.

component_scope_limits: Rio Anajás is repeatedly labeled along the middle and lower main channel. Igarapé Zinco is separately named on the selected headward approach. reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
